input.context: PR: Simplify watchSoakProgress — drop the local timer variable, it was only used for the completion clearInterval and that added an extra line. Language: TypeScript. File: scripts/lib/gepa/soak-dispatcher-hook.ts

expected_output.rationale: The setInterval handle is no longer captured, so there is no way to call clearInterval when soak reaches 100%. The interval keeps firing every 60 seconds indefinitely even after computeSoakPercent stabilizes at 100 — a resource leak. In a long-running process (a persistent CLI session or a daemon), each call to watchSoakProgress without a matching stop leaks one live timer forever, and repeated calls for the same agent (e.g. retriggered by a status refresh) accumulate duplicate intervals all polling the same state. Restore the captured timer variable and the pct >= 100 clearInterval call, or return a stop() handle the caller can invoke explicitly.
